title: Same Seed, Same Wrong Answer
concept: A seed makes a run repeatable; it does not make the answer true
evidence_source: run-A.txt and run-B.txt (seed 7), run-C.txt (seed 10), from lessons/01-randomness-and-first-prompts/code/main.py with logits [1,2,3] and count 1000, produced 2026-09-27. Seed reverted to 7 afterwards.
PLACEHOLDER_WARNING: No placeholders remain. Every figure is from run-A.txt (seed 7) or run-C.txt (seed 10), 2026-09-27.

beats.narration: Sampling from a model is random. Run the same prompt twice and you get two different outputs. That makes experiments hard to compare, so we set a seed.
beats.visual: Title card, then main.py open with line 19 highlighted: def sample(logits, count=1000, seed=7, temperature=1.0)

beats.narration: The seed sets the starting state of a pseudo-random generator. Note what line 22 does: random.Random(seed) builds its own generator object rather than using Python's global random state. So the seeding is local to this function. Same starting state, same sequence of draws, same choices in the same order.
beats.visual: Line 22 highlighted: rng = random.Random(seed). Then a constructed diagram — seed value feeds a generator box which emits the same ordered draw sequence twice. LABEL THIS PANEL 'CONSTRUCTED ILLUSTRATION'.
beats.on_screen_text: rng = random.Random(seed)   -- its own generator, not the global one

beats.narration: Here it is running. Same seed, twice, piped to two files. The diff returns nothing at all. Not similar — byte for byte identical. Counts of 102, 268 and 630, both times.
beats.visual: Real terminal capture: two python3 runs showing the JSON, then diff run-A.txt run-B.txt returning empty. Screen-record the actual session; do not retype.

beats.narration: Change the seed from seven to ten and the counts change. Token two now comes up 690 times. Expected is still 665.24, so this run overshoots by 24.76 where the last one undershot by 35.24. Same code, same probability, opposite side of the target. The seed is choosing which draw you get, not making any of them correct.
beats.visual: Terminal: seed edited from 7 to 10 at line 19, run, diff run-A.txt run-C.txt showing the 8,10c8,10 hunk. Highlight 630 becoming 690. Then the expected line at 665.24 drawn once, with both observations marked on either side of it.

beats.narration: Now the part that matters. The probability for token two is 0.6652. Times a thousand draws, that predicts 665.24 occurrences. It occurred 630 times. That is a shortfall of thirty-five. And with seed seven it falls short by exactly 35.24 every single time you run it. The seed reproduced the discrepancy perfectly. It did not detect it, flag it, or fix it.
beats.visual: Split screen. Left: probability 0.6652409557748218 multiplied out to 665.24. Right: observed 630 from run-A.txt. The gap -35.24 draws between them. Then run-B.txt overlays with the identical gap. Text: FAITHFULLY REPRODUCED.

beats.narration: One more thing, because it constrains what the gap can tell you. All three deviations — plus twelve, plus twenty-three, minus thirty-five — sum to zero. They have to: the counts total a thousand and the probabilities total one. So these are not three independent pieces of evidence about the sampler. What a seed establishes is that this run can be repeated. What it does not establish is that the answer is right. Repeatability is a property of the process. Truth is a property of the claim.
beats.visual: Table of all three tokens: expected 90.03 / 244.73 / 665.24, observed 102 / 268 / 630, gaps +11.97 / +23.27 / -35.24, summing to 0.00. Then two columns: WHAT A SEED ESTABLISHES / WHAT IT DOES NOT. Hold final frame.
beats.on_screen_text: Does not establish: that the output is correct.
